subject: physics
question_text: Name the seven fundamental quantities in the SI system and write their units.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The seven quantities
lines: The seven fundamental quantities are length,
amount of substance and luminous intensity.
steps.why: These seven are independent of one another, so no one of them can be built from the rest. Every other unit in the SI system is built from these.
common_mistakes: Including force or energy. Both are derived, not fundamental.

recall.must_convey: That the seven are length, mass, time, current, temperature, amount of substance and luminous intensity.

steps.memory_tip: Three mechanical (length, mass, time) then four more: current, temperature, amount of substance, luminous intensity. Their units: ampere, kelvin, mole, candela.
steps.margin_note: Count to seven before you stop writing.

steps.label: Their units
lines: These seven are the SI base units.
steps.why: Pairing each unit with its quantity in the same order is what shows the list was understood rather than remembered as loose words.
common_mistakes: Writing degree Celsius for temperature. The base unit is the kelvin.
Writing gram instead of kilogram. The base unit carries the kilo.

recall.must_convey: That the units are metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole and candela.

steps.memory_tip: Kelvin not Celsius, kilogram not gram. Those are the two that get dropped marks.
steps.margin_note: Keep the order the same as the quantities above.

insider_note: Seven pairs, two marks. Write them as a list of quantity and unit — a missing unit costs the second mark.
